gaps.sentence: ___ the fact that costs had doubled, the project was allowed to continue.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the fact that' = although, in a more formal wrapper.

gaps.sentence: He talks ___ he owned the place.
gaps.explanation: 'As if/though + past' describes behaviour contrary to fact (he doesn't own it).

gaps.sentence: ___ his salary, he earns royalties from three textbooks.
gaps.explanation: 'In addition to + noun' adds one source of income to another.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: She has decided to cycle to work ___ taking the bus.
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + -ing' = in place of the bus journey.

gaps.sentence: It sounds ___ the negotiations are close to a breakthrough.
gaps.explanation: 'It sounds as though...' reports an impression.

gaps.sentence: The expedition will go ahead ___ the sponsors confirm the funding.
gaps.explanation: 'Provided that' = only if, a formal positive condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ her age, she still runs marathons.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + noun (her age); the conjunctions would need a clause.
